# Jane Andrews

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c11 P18](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0018)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c11 P18](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0018), [v1 c15 P2](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0002)</sub>
- **Role:** Teacher  <sub>[v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024)</sub>

## Appearance

Jane is a plain, neat girl with a stout figure. During her graduation from the domestic science course, she wore a white satin dress adorned with seed pearls, tulle, lace, and a diamond cluster engagement ring.

_Sources: [v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c1 P17](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0017), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v3 c2 P12](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0012)_

## Personality

Jane is a practical, sensible, and matter-of-fact girl with little imagination. She is neat, industrious, and conscientious in her work, preferring order and straightforward methods. Though she lacks an artistic or poetical nature, she is loyal, sweet-tempered, and well-behaved.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001), [v1 c17 P19](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0019), [v1 c26 P13](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0013), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c36 P18](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0018), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059)_

## History

Jane grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school with Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, forming a close friendship with them. She later studied at Queen's Academy to become a teacher, subsequently taking the Second Class teacher's course at Redmond College. After graduating, Jane accepted a teaching position in Newbridge. She joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and participated in various community events and the girl's Story Club, though her own stories were strictly sensible and free from romance. She was later offered a teaching position out West, where she went to teach. While there, she became engaged to Edward Inglis, a wealthy Winnipeg millionaire, and married him at her family home in Avonlea before leaving for a wedding tour in Europe and settling in a Winnipeg mansion.
